newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares up in early bourse on firm dollar.
newsitem.headline: German shares up in early bourse on firm dollar.

text.p: German equities continued to register strong gains in early bourse trade on Monday, lifted by the continuing strength of the dollar, which one trader described as "staggering".

However, there were indications that the market was experiencing a bout of vertigo at such lofty heights and dealers said the DAX index of 30 German blue-chips would have to consolidate sooner rather than later.
In early bourse trade the DAX stood at 3,019.36 points, up 17.99 points or 0.60 percent.

"These are frightening times. The strength of the dollar is staggering, which is underpinning everything. We need to be careful -- the markets are close to busting through year-end forecasts and it's only January," said one trader.
Fundamental factors expected to move the market this week include M3 money supply figures and German producer prices data for December, both expected early this week.
Dealers said they would also be monitoring the Ifo report on German business sentiment, also due early in the week.
Shares in the news include Deutsche Telekom AG, up 48 pfennigs at 31.60 marks.

Telekom was lifted by its announcement that sales grew to more than 63 billion marks, that it would pay as promised a dividend of 60 pfennigs per share on 1996 results and that it cut debt by 10 billion marks.

There was also keen interest in the banking sector. Deutsche Bank AG was up 1.12 marks at 80 marks, Commerzbank was up 29 pfennigs at 44.10 marks and Dresdner Bank AG was up 1.10 marks at 53.20 marks.
